caption: Observer + sticky piston T flip-flop, 4 blocks (found by the tff census): a sticky piston P facing down (powered by the input) has an observer O watching it from the east, and a sticky piston Q two cells east of P's foot faces west at a redstone block R; Q is quasi-connected through the cell O outputs into. Each input pulse makes P extend and retract, so O pulses twice: with R next to Q (output on), Q's first short pulse pushes R under P and spits it there; with R under P, P pushes it down and pulls it back, Q's head reaches out and the second observer pulse pulls R home. Latency 11 gt, pulses of 3 gt and longer, trains down to a 10 gt period; rests ON.

Powder snow dispenser T flip-flop, dust variant, 7 blocks (track tff): the dispenser of tff-snowdisp (each pulse places or picks up powder snow, the dispenser holding a powder snow bucket or an empty bucket); its comparator gives 2 or 1, and two dust decay that to 1 or 0. Latency 6 gt, 1 gt pulses, trains down to 4 gt; rests ON.

Powder snow dispenser T flip-flop, 6 blocks (track tff): each input pulse fires a dispenser facing up; it holds a powder snow bucket (it places powder snow above itself and keeps an empty bucket) or an empty bucket (it picks the powder snow back up). Comparator C reads the dispenser: 2 with the powder snow bucket (stack size 1), 1 with the empty bucket (stack size 16); comparator K feeds C's side a constant 2 read from a dropper holding a powder snow bucket, so C (compare mode) gives 2 or 0. Latency 6 gt (dispenser 4 + comparator 2), 1 gt pulses, trains down to 4 gt; rests ON.

Dropper ring T flip-flop, 8 blocks (track tff): droppers D1 and D2 at opposite corners of a 2x2 ring, each passing to a hopper that passes on to the other dropper; one stone. The input fires both droppers (D1 directly, D2 through two dust on the hopper and on D2); only the one holding the stone moves it, into its hopper, which delivers it to the other dropper 7 gt later, after both have fired, so the order in which the two droppers fire never matters (two droppers facing each other would pass the stone back in the same tick). A comparator reads D2. Latency 13 gt, 1 gt pulses, trains down to 12 gt.

Crafter T flip-flop, 8 blocks (track tff): a crafter holding nine iron ingots faces a hopper that feeds back into it. A pulse crafts an iron block into the hopper, which hands it back 8 gt later; the next pulse crafts the block back into nine ingots, which the hopper returns one by one (the crafter spreads them over its nine slots, ready for the next block). A comparator reads the crafter (filled slots: 9 or 1) and two dust turn that into 8 or 0; the output is back on once two ingots have returned. Latency 21 gt, 1 gt pulses; the ingot return (72 gt) makes it slow (min period over 30 gt).

Piston + slime T flip-flop, 5 blocks (found by the tff census): sticky piston s (facing east, next to the input) has a slime block and a redstone block R in front; a piston p under R faces back west (R powers it: extended at rest) and a piston P under s faces east (quasi-powered by the input through s's cell). ON: s pushes slime + R east (R over the output cell), p loses R and retracts, P extends into the gap; when the input falls s cannot pull the slime back (it would drag p into P's head), P retracts and p, now quasi-powered through the slime, extends again. OFF: s extends into the empty cell and, on the falling edge, pulls slime + R back (the extended p is immovable and stays). Latency 5 gt, 1 gt pulses, trains down to a 5 gt period.

Observer + piston line T flip-flop, 5 blocks (found by the tff census): the input piston P pushes a sticky piston S2 and its redstone block R east; after the first pulse R alternates between the output cell itself (off) and the cell beyond it (on). Under P, a sticky piston shuttles an observer under S2 and back on every pulse, and S2 alternately spits R one cell out (short power) and pulls it back. Latency 5 gt, 4 gt pulses and longer, trains down to an 8 gt period.

Observer + slime + two sticky pistons T flip-flop, flat, 5 blocks (found by the tff census): sticky piston s (next to the input, facing south) has a redstone block R in front of it; an observer watching s fires a second sticky piston A (through the slime block it outputs into) on both edges of each pulse. One pulse leaves R in front of s (output off), the next has A pull R over the output cell (on), whose next pulse pushes it back. All in one layer. Latency 7 gt (on the falling edge), 3 gt pulses and longer, trains down to a 10 gt period.

Repeater-lock master-slave T flip-flop, redstone only, 24 blocks (track tff): master repeater M feeds slave repeater S; M is locked while the input is on (a repeater fed by a dust from the input), S while it is off (a repeater reading a stone that a dust, kept straight by a redstone block, points into, until the input next to that dust bends it into a corner). S's output powers a stone whose torch (NOT q) runs back along four dust into M, so M holds NOT q while the input is off and S copies it on the rising edge.

Single-latch pulse-window T flip-flop, redstone only, 17 blocks (track tff, shrunk from a master-slave by a lock census): repeater M holds q; its lock C (a comparator) reads a dust A that the input powers while on and that a stone powers while off (through a subtract comparator with a redstone block behind it: NOT input). That stone takes 2 gt to come back after the falling edge, so A and C drop for one short window and M copies its own inverse once: M powers stone B, two dust carry q to stone K, and K's torch (NOT q) stands right behind M. Latency 4 gt (falling edge), 2 gt pulses, trains down to a 4 gt period.

Crafter T flip-flop, 7 blocks (track tff): a crafter holding nine iron ingots faces a hopper that feeds back into it. A pulse crafts an iron block into the hopper, which hands it back 8 gt later; the next pulse crafts the block back into nine ingots, which the hopper returns one by one (the crafter spreads them over its nine slots). A subtract comparator reads the crafter (filled slots: 9 or 1) minus a constant 1 (a comparator reading a dropper that holds one stone), so the output is 8 or 0 once the ingots are back.

Copper bulb T flip-flop, 3 blocks (track tff): the input (a redstone block written next to it) powers a waxed copper bulb, which toggles LIT on every rising edge of its power, in the update itself; a comparator on stone reads the bulb (15 / 0) and the output is the cell it points into: latency 2 gt (the comparator), 1 gt pulses accepted, trains down to 2 gt periods followed. A row of them tiles at pitch 2 along z (`tile: 0 0 2`): pitch 1 is impossible, because then the comparators sit side by side and a comparator's side input suppresses its neighbour (ComparatorBlock.getAlternateSignal), which the judge measures as latency 9 gt instead of 2.
